attribution: Revealed to Vasugupta according to tradition, which holds that he found them inscribed on a rock or received them in a dream
author: vasugupta
period: Commonly dated to the 9th century CE
summary: A set of 77 terse aphorisms at the root of Kashmir Shaivism, describing consciousness as the Self and the means of realising it.
whyRead: It is the foundational scripture of the non-dual Shaiva traditions of Kashmir. Its classification of means (upayas) remains a key framework for Trika thought and practice.
questions: What binds consciousness, and how is it freed?
Are there different paths for different temperaments?

keyTeachings.title: Consciousness is the Self
keyTeachings.text: The first sutra identifies the Self with consciousness (chaitanya), understood as dynamic and free, not merely a passive witness.

keyTeachings.title: Bondage as limited knowing
keyTeachings.text: Bondage is traced to limited or contracted knowledge and to the powers that veil consciousness from itself.

keyTeachings.title: Three means (upayas)
keyTeachings.text: The sutras are divided according to three means: the divine means (shambhavopaya) of sudden recognition, the empowered means (shaktopaya) of refined awareness, and the individual means (anavopaya) using breath, body and concentration.

keyTeachings.title: Effort as Bhairava
keyTeachings.text: An early sutra identifies the upsurge of awareness (udyama) with Bhairava, the supreme Shiva, suggesting that realisation arises in a flash of awakened attention.

passages.about: The upsurge of awareness identified with Bhairava
